jobs.match_text: postdoc on higgs boson physics with atlas the atlas group at lpsc grenoble is opening a two-year (plus possible extension) post-doc position to work on the atlas experiment, with a focus on the measurement of higgs pair production, expected to start in summer 2026. the laboratoire de physique subatomique et de cosmologie (lpsc) in grenoble ( http://lpsc.in2p3.fr ), is a joint research unit of cnrs-in2p3, université grenoble alpes (uga), and grenoble inp. the lpsc is strongly involved in particle, astroparticle and nuclear physics, cosmology and theory phenomenology, as well as their applications and developments for nuclear energy and safety, and accelerator physics. the selected candidate will join the atlas group, composed by 9 staff members of the lpsc, and under the coordination of the atlas group leader. the group has a long-term involvement in detector construction, in particular for the atlas liquid argon calorimeter. for the phase-2 upgrade (2027-2030), the group has a strong involvement in the construction of the upgraded all-silicon inner tracking system (itk) for the atlas detector. the atlas group has a strong record in jet reconstruction and calibration, and electron and photon performance, as well as physics data analysis, with a focus on higgs boson physics, exotic searches in the dark qcd sector, and top physics. this postdoc position is opened in the framework of the physics program “studying the higgs sector with atlas at the lhc and prospects for the future circular collider” financed by a cpj cnrs position, which includes the recruitment with the lpsc atlas group of one phd student and one postdoc during the period of 2025-2029, with a focus on the study of multi-higgs production processes, supported by two lpsc agents. the successful candidate for this position will work in collaboration with this group. the successful candidate will join the atlas group at the lpsc. the candidate will work on the analysis of data collected by the atlas experiment during the lhc run-3, for the search of higgs boson pair production (hh) in the decay channel to bottom quark and tau lepton pairs. the main goal of this research will be the publication of the results for this analysis using the entirety of the lhc run-3 dataset. part of the research work could consist in the deployment of novel tau lepton identification algorithms, as well as the optimization of the trigger strategy in the hh analysis. the possibility to extend this research axis to the study of hh production in boosted regimes in the decay channel to bottom quarks and tau leptons is foreseen, as well as the preparation of the statistical combination of multi-higgs measurements with the whole lhc run-3 dataset. the atlas lpsc group has a strong commitment in the construction of the upgrade for the atlas inner tracker detector (itk) for the high-luminosity lhc phase. the candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to the production of solid competencies to work in collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment. the position is for a period of 24 months, with the possibility of an extension, and it is based at the lpsc in grenoble. regular trips to cern are foreseen in the context of the research project, to participate to collaboration meetings and possibly to detector operations. the lpsc is strongly committed to jobs.title: Postdoctoral Position at the LHCb Experiment
jobs.match_text: postdoctoral position at the lhcb experiment the lhcb group at peking university invites applications for a postdoctoral research position. we are seeking highly motivated candidates to join our team and contribute to the exciting physics program of the lhcb experiment. the primary focus of this position is on the software r&d for upgrade of the electromagnetic calorimeter (ecal) for the high-luminosity lhc (hl-lhc) era. the upgraded ecal will feature high-granularity spaghetti calorimeter (spacal) technology for the inner region and shashlik modules for the outer region, with precision hit-timing measurements achieving resolutions on the order of tens of picoseconds. about the group since joining the lhcb collaboration in 2019, the peking university team has been actively involved in both key physics analyses and detector r&d, with contributions in both hardware and software. our group has achieved a series of important results in frontier research areas such as cp violation, hadron spectroscopy, heavy-flavor production mechanisms, and the search for new physics beyond the standard model. currently, the team is playing a significant role in the r&d of the ecal upgrade for the lhcb detector. job description the primary responsibility of the successful candidate will be to work on software and simulation tasks for the ecal upgrade project. this includes developing and optimizing simulation software, contributing to algorithm development (potentially involving machine learning techniques), and validating the performance of new calorimeter designs. conditions the initial contract is for two years, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and mutual agreement. the position is based at peking university in beijing, china, with regular opportunities for travel to cern. the annual gross salary (before-tax) is 340,000 cny (approx. 42,000 eur / 49,000 usd), which serves as a competitive baseline. this is complemented by a performance-based year-end bonus, as well as additional allowances for travel to cern. besides, candidates are encouraged to apply for the university-supported fellowship program. successful applicants will receive a significantly enhanced compensation package. the expected start date is as soon as possible, but the exact starting time is flexible and can be negotiated. candidate profile a ph.d. in experimental particle physics or a closely related field. proven experience in high-energy physics data analysis and/or detector software and simulation. strong teamwork skills and the ability to work effectively in a large, international collaboration. solid programming skills (c++ and python are essential). desirable qualifications: prior experience with calorimeter systems (especially electromagnetic calorimeters) and/or experience with machine learning applications in physics. application process interested candidates should prepare the following application materials: a curriculum vitae (cv), including a list of publications. a cover letter describing your research interests, relevant experience, and motivation for applying. contact information for at least two referees, who should be willing to send letters of recommendation directly to the contact email below. all application materials (except reference letters) should be combined into a single pdf file and sent via email. reference letters should be sent directly to the same address. review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

the successful candidate is also expected to take part in physics analyses compatible with our research program and to help with the supervision of our students. the position could be located at cern jobs.title: Postdoctoral positions in particle physics phenomenology
jobs.match_text: postdoctoral positions in particle physics phenomenology applications are invited for a few postdoctoral positions in the particle physics phenomenology group at the institute of quantum matter, south china normal university, guangzhou, china. the institute was founded in 2018, and has established research groups in high energy nuclear theory, hadron physics, high energy experiments, lattice field theory, particle physics phenomenology (ppp), and quantum field theory. the ppp group currently consists of three faculty members (yi liao, yu jia, and xiao-dong ma), and a few postdocs and phd students. the group has close academic connections to cold-atom and quantum physics groups in the school of physics as well as other groups in the institute. the current interest of yi liao and xiao-dong ma covers most of the topics related to neutrino physics, dark matter, tests of baryon- and lepton-number violation from low-energy processes, and collider physics, emphasizing the effective field theory approach to physics beyond the standard model. in the meanwhile, they are developing research topics in strong field physics, physics with twisted particles, and effective theory in other disciplines such as condensed matter, atomic, and optical physics. yu jia's research interest includes the application of various effective field theory approaches to qcd phenomenology, such as hqet, nrqcd, scet, lamet, and chiral perturbation theory. his work also involves investigating the effects of higher-order radiative corrections on hadron structure, as well as studying nonperturbative aspects of solvable lower-dimensional quantum field theories. furthermore, he is interested in extending effective field theory techniques to novel settings, including strong-field physics and atomic physics. the appointment is for two or three years upon evaluation and performance, and is expected to start in fall 2026 or earlier upon negotiation. successful postdocs will be paid on an internationally competitive level, and will get some support for attending workshops. all postdocs are encouraged to collaborate with the members of the ppp group as well as other groups in the institute, and are eligible to apply for grants to the china postdoctoral science foundation and the national natural science foundation of china. applicants should send a curriculum vitae (including birthday and phd dates), a list of publications, and a research plan, and arrange for at least two reference letters to be sent directly by the referees. the review will start immediately, and will continue until the positions are filled.

jobs.match_text: postdoctoral fellowship in experimental particle and strong-field qed physics the wis hep-ex group is seeking a postdoc to take leading a role in forefront strong-field qed experiments across world-leading laboratories, including slac (e320, us), desy (luxe, germany), eli-np (romania), apollon (france) and possibly corels (korea). these experiments are designed to test qed at ultra intense electric fields using collisions of ~10 gev accelerated electrons (linac or lwf) and ~0.01-10 pw laser pulses. the schwinger critical field is approached and physical processes of pure non-perturbative nature may be observed. in all experiments mentioned above, the wis group is responsible for the pixel tracking detectors - the central systems for measuring the elusive non-linear breit-wheeler e+e- pair production in the tunneling regime, possibly for the first time. we also participate in the overall design, construction, operation and simulation of the experiments, as well as the physics-analysis. for more context on our recent work, please see nim. a. 1083, mar 2026, 171144 and arxiv:2604.23805 (apr 2026) for e320, and epj. spec. top. 233, candidate will drive the implementation of novel radiation mechanisms that leverage the interaction between free electrons and novel nanomaterials and nanostructured media. this role is ideal for a "builder" who thrives on integrating complex vacuum systems with advanced electron-optical components to achieve high-brightness emission in the short-wavelength regime. this is a high-visibility role involves translating theoretical breakthroughs into functional, scalable prototypes with applications in semiconductor lithography, metrology, and beyond. key responsibilities: · experimental platform high-fidelity measurements of brightness and coherence. · hardware integration: collaborate with theorists and fabrication experts to integrate functional nanostructures into experimental vacuum environments. · laboratory leadership: manage experimental workflows, oversee lab safety, and provide technical mentorship to phd and msc students. prerequisites & expertise o phd and prior beam-matter interactions. o vacuum systems specialist: proficient in the design and maintenance of ultra-high vacuum (uhv) systems. o preferred (but not mandatory) skills: - experience in the euv or soft x-ray regime (e.g., photo-emission, synchrotron beamlines, or hhg). - familiarity with euv detectors (ccds, mcps) and grazing incidence optics. - experience with nanofabrication or characterization of photonic nanostructures. - mindset: a "builder" mentality—highly independent, hands-on, and capable of troubleshooting complex, first-of-their-kind experimental systems. why join
